active_paradigms.idea: Solve an exact set-partitioning formulation over feasible GPU configurations with scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program is demand-first greedy placement followed by monotone one-model moves and pairwise swaps; it is strong because every accepted edit improves the true maximum KVPR, but it cannot cross a temporary worsening move or a multi-model rearrangement. Exploit that GPUs are identical by enumerating each feasible subset of models whose total size is strictly below 80 GB as a candidate GPU configuration. For every configuration, precompute its exact pressure as sum(req_rate/slo) divided by 80 minus total model_size. Create one binary MILP variable per configuration and require every model to occur in exactly one selected configuration, while selecting at most gpu_num configurations. Add an epigraph variable z and constraints z >= pressure(configuration) times each selected configuration variable, then minimize z in one scipy.optimize.milp call. Include an empty configuration with pressure zero so unused GPUs are represented without special cases. This directly optimizes the evaluator's per-instance maximum KVPR rather than a load-only surrogate, and can find coordinated repartitions unreachable by moves and swaps.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The actual maximum KVPR on each generated case, which is the quantity averaged and inverted by the evaluator; reducing high-pressure outlier GPUs is more important than improving average per-GPU load.
active_paradigms.cautions: Full subset enumeration is exponential, so use this exact method only when model count is modest or prune subsets immediately once memory reaches 80 GB. Memory feasibility must remain strict (< 80), not <= 80, because a zero denominator produces infinite pressure. Avoid retaining numerically dominated duplicate configurations, but do not discard a configuration merely because its standalone pressure is high if it is needed to cover a large model. Use a finite safe upper bound for z and verify the selected patterns cover every original model exactly once before constructing the returned placement.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.brute for exact direct search over canonical GPU assignments on small instances
active_paradigms.description: Unlike the current greedy-plus-local-search algorithm, scipy.optimize.brute can evaluate the exact nonlinear objective of every assignment in a small instance and therefore is not restricted to locally improving moves. Represent a candidate as an integer GPU index for each model, decode it into GPU model lists, and calculate the same maximum KVPR used by the evaluator. Return a very large finite objective for any candidate where a GPU has total model size greater than or equal to 80 GB, so invalid assignments can never win. Remove GPU-label symmetry before the brute call by fixing the first model to GPU zero and rejecting assignments whose first use of a GPU is not in sequential order. Sort models by decreasing size or pressure contribution before encoding so infeasible assignments are rejected quickly and equivalent cases are reduced. Use brute only below a conservative state-space limit, such as when gpu_num^(model_count-1) is comfortably bounded; otherwise retain the existing fast placement method. This is an exact objective-level benchmark and can reveal whether the local-search score gap is due to true local minima rather than its initial ordering.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Exact minimization of the evaluator's nonlinear maximum KVPR for small cases, with special emphasis on finding global rearrangements involving three or more GPUs.
active_paradigms.cautions: The grid grows exponentially, so a hard instance-size cutoff is mandatory to avoid evaluator timeout. The invalid objective must be finite and larger than every plausible feasible pressure, because infinities can cause optimizer comparison problems. Ensure all GPU keys are returned even for empty GPUs. This is most useful as a small-instance exact solver, not as an unconditional replacement for the current heuristic.

active_paradigms.idea: Use mixed-integer global differential evolution with scipy.optimize.differential_evolution to escape multi-model local minima
active_paradigms.description: The existing algorithm evaluates only one transfer and one cross-GPU swap at a time, so it stops whenever lowering the bottleneck requires a cyclic or temporarily worsening reassignment. Encode every model's destination GPU as an integer decision variable and have the objective decode all assignments and compute the exact maximum KVPR. scipy.optimize.differential_evolution supports an integrality mask, allowing every coordinate to remain an integer GPU label rather than using a rounded continuous local optimizer. Assign a large finite penalty to placements with any total size at or above 80 GB, optionally scaling the penalty by the amount of overflow so the search is directed back toward feasibility. Seed the population with the current program's placement and several demand-first or size-first assignments, then perform a single direct global optimization call with polishing disabled. Since the objective is the exact bottleneck pressure, accepted global candidates need not rely on a surrogate balancing criterion. This is particularly promising for medium-sized instances where full configuration enumeration is too large but the current move/swap neighborhood is visibly restrictive.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduction of the worst GPU KVPR through coordinated reassignment of several models, while preserving feasible positive residual memory on every GPU.
active_paradigms.cautions: Use integer bounds [0, gpu_num-1] and the integrality parameter; do not decode arbitrary fractional coordinates by ad hoc rounding. Keep population size and maxiter tightly bounded for the evaluator timeout, and make the objective deterministic. Penalties must reject residual memory of zero as well as negative residual memory. Differential evolution is heuristic, so always compare its final decoded placement against the current greedy-local-search placement and return the better feasible one.

tried_paradigms.idea: Exact set-partitioning minimax solver using scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a demand-first greedy assignment followed by monotone best-improvement single moves and pairwise swaps. Its strength is that every accepted operation directly lowers the true maximum KVPR and swaps repair some packing conflicts, but it cannot cross a temporary worsening barrier and cannot perform multi-model exchanges. Replace the heuristic by a configuration set-partitioning formulation when the number of models is moderate. Deterministically enumerate every subset of models whose total model size is strictly below 80 GB; each subset is one feasible GPU configuration with a known load, residual memory, and fixed KVPR. Add one binary variable per configuration, require every model to occur in exactly one chosen configuration, and require exactly gpu_num configurations, including an empty configuration to represent unused GPUs. Encode minimax selection by also choosing one KVPR threshold from the sorted distinct configuration pressures, allowing only configurations at or below that chosen threshold, and minimize the selected threshold in one MILP call. This optimizes the evaluator's actual per-GPU ratio globally rather than optimizing a surrogate load balance. It is particularly valuable on instances where the greedy placement needs a 3-way or larger rearrangement to expose a lower-pressure packing.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimize the maximum of sum(req_rate/slo) divided by remaining GPU memory, which is the quantity whose cross-GPU maximum drives the reported score; feasibility and exact model coverage are hard constraints.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Subset enumeration is exponential, so use it only when model count and feasible-subset count are modest, and use a deterministic cutoff/fallback for large instances. Do not include subsets with total size equal to 80 because they have zero residual memory and infinite KVPR; preserve the current program's strict fit convention. Configuration variables may select identical empty configurations multiple times, which is necessary when gpu_num exceeds the number of nonempty groups. Build threshold/configuration incidence constraints carefully so a selected configuration is forbidden whenever its fixed pressure exceeds the selected threshold.

tried_paradigms.idea: Direct integer global search over assignments with scipy.optimize.differential_evolution
tried_paradigms.description: Use SciPy's differential_evolution in its integer-variable mode to optimize a vector containing one GPU index for each model, with the objective evaluated directly from the induced placement. The current greedy-plus-local-search solution is an excellent deterministic seed because its weakness is not objective evaluation but its restricted one-move/one-swap neighborhood. Set bounds of [0, gpu_num-1] for every assignment coordinate and set integrality=True for all coordinates, then evaluate the exact maximum KVPR after grouping models by their candidate GPU. Return a very large finite penalty for any assignment having total size at least 80 GB on a GPU, rather than allowing division by zero or exceptions. Seed the initial population with the current greedy placement and several demand-balanced/random feasible assignments, while retaining differential evolution as the single direct optimization call. The solver can alter many model assignments simultaneously, so it can discover coordinated repackings that are inaccessible to monotonic local search. Use the final integer assignment itself as the placement, with no continuous relaxation or rounding stage.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The exact maximum final KVPR, with infeasible memory assignments made decisively worse than every feasible placement; this targets coordinated global reassignment rather than only local improvement.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This is appropriate only if the installed SciPy supports differential_evolution's integrality argument; otherwise do not silently round continuous coordinates during objective evaluation because that creates large flat regions. Use a finite but safely dominant infeasibility penalty and explicitly reject residual memory <= 0. Runtime grows quickly with number of models, so cap popsize and maxiter based on evaluator limits and favor a seeded population. GPU labels are symmetric, so canonicalizing equivalent assignments in the objective cache can substantially reduce repeated work if caching is permitted.

tried_paradigms.idea: Exact exhaustive assignment selection with itertools.product for small hidden instances
tried_paradigms.description: For genuinely small cases, use itertools.product(range(gpu_num), repeat=len(models)) to enumerate every complete discrete placement and retain the feasible candidate with the smallest exact maximum KVPR. This is fundamentally different from the current method: it has no greedy ordering bias, no local-neighborhood restriction, and therefore certifies the global optimum for cases within its search budget. During each candidate evaluation, accumulate model sizes and weights per GPU, reject immediately if any used GPU has residual memory less than or equal to zero, and otherwise compute the same load/residual ratio as the evaluator. Empty GPUs contribute zero pressure, so they need no special balancing rule. A practical deterministic guard can select this method only when gpu_num ** len(models) is below a conservative operation budget; otherwise return the existing greedy-and-swap result. On distributions containing small but difficult combinatorial instances, exact enumeration can improve the average score disproportionately because it removes all heuristic error on those cases. Unlike a fractional flow or slot approximation, every retained candidate is a valid indivisible model placement and is scored by the true objective.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Obtain the globally minimal maximum KVPR on small instances, eliminating the current heuristic's failure modes from those evaluator cases while preserving exact memory feasibility.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The search space is gpu_num to the power of model count, so the guard is essential; do not attempt this indiscriminately on large inputs. Evaluate using strict residual-memory positivity, not merely total size <= 80, to avoid infinite pressure. Symmetry can be reduced by fixing the first model on GPU 0 or by canonical GPU-label generation, but any pruning must not exclude feasible unlabeled partitions. Ensure the fallback remains deterministic and returns the required dictionary keyed by every GPU index.
